sites.downstream: response.content[0].text stripped and returned as bare label string; one of 10 insurance categories. No metadata (usage, finish_reason, IDs) consumed or returned.
sites.reason: Closed 10-label classification over short insurance tickets from a benign fixed corpus. No math, date comparison, multi-hop reasoning, generation, or adversarial input. Semantic categorization is a textbook Jev Choice use case.

options.benefit: Lower cost and latency on accepted decisions. Jev input-token pricing ($0.042/Mtok) is substantially cheaper than Claude Haiku ($0.80/Mtok input). Most tickets should classify at high confidence, avoiding the Claude call entirely. Expected cost = Jev cost + fallback_fraction * Claude cost.
options.risk: Serial miss adds Jev latency before Claude fallback — total latency increases on low-confidence inputs. Jev and Claude may disagree on ambiguous tickets; threshold tuning needed on representative data.

options.benefit: Removes Claude dependency and cost entirely. Maximum cost and latency savings.
options.risk: Residual classification errors with no safety net. Excluded by conservative risk posture.

options.benefit: No change, no risk. Original behavior preserved exactly.
